audience: Adults comparing commercial program features; not treatment selection
conclusion: Use the checklist to narrow questions, then discuss treatment decisions, risks, and eligibility with a qualified healthcare professional.
direct_answer: Compare total price, product and pharmacy disclosures, prescribing and follow-up process, insurance support, shipping, cancellation terms, and evidence freshness. Do not treat a program comparison as medical advice or eligibility screening.
h1: How to compare online GLP-1 providers without guessing
primary_keyword: how to compare online glp-1 providers

sections.heading: Start with total cost, not a headline price
paragraphs: Ask whether the displayed price includes intake, clinician visits, medication, supplies, shipping, lab work, and follow-up. A low teaser price is not comparable with an all-in program unless each component and renewal cadence is clear.
Record the source URL and checked date for every price. If a provider does not publish an all-in amount, label the field unknown rather than estimating it.

sections.heading: Separate branded FDA-approved products from compounded products
paragraphs: A comparison must identify the product category without implying that a compounded drug is FDA-approved or a generic equivalent. Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. Availability and legal conditions can change, so the source date matters.

sections.heading: Check oversight, support, shipping, and cancellation
paragraphs: Commercial pages should describe the documented process rather than promise a result. Verify the stated prescribing workflow, follow-up cadence, support channel, shipping area, refund or cancellation terms, and insurance-assistance claims from current primary pages.
